body.statement: There exist universal constants \(a_0,A_0\) such that, for every \(n,T\geq1\) and \(c\in[0,1]\), \(a_0/n\leq R^{\mathrm{or}}(n,T,c)\leq A_0/n\) and \(a_0/\sqrt n\leq L^{\mathrm{or}}(n,T,c)\leq A_0/\sqrt n\). The upper procedures are clipped inverse-likelihood weighting and its Chebyshev interval, and the lower bounds use a Bernoulli terminal-outcome subexperiment.
body.justification: A uniform parametric oracle benchmark makes any unknown-history penalty an information effect rather than exploding intervention weights.
body.gap: KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies compares local efficiency bounds under structured policy models; it does not give this all-sample unrestricted-history oracle decision bound.
body.consumer: The oracle comparison tells longitudinal analysts whether supplying a fitted propensity tree could change the order of attainable precision.
